title: Punt 3PTM: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt 3PTM build in our league, grouped into tiers with what each adds in FG%, REB and BLK? It must note that threes are easy to find on waivers, so non-shooters lose less than rankings suggest.
summary: Punting 3PTM costs our league less than the rankings suggest. About two threes a game is now average, and three-point specialists are easy to find on waivers. Build around Amen Thompson, Jalen Duren, Dyson Daniels and Ausar Thompson, then fill out the roster with cheap starting centers for FG%, REB and BLK, and keep a waiver list of big men for FAB.

sections.heading: Why punting threes costs less here

paragraphs.text: The experts agree that threes are easy to find on the waiver wire. Do not overvalue threes in the draft, because three-point specialists can be picked up later. Non-shooters are not hurt much in threes for the same reason. A player's overall rank counts his lack of threes against him, but in our league that loss is cheaper than the rank suggests.

The baseline for threes has also gone up. About two threes a game is now average in fantasy, so a shooter who hits only two is nothing special. At our 18 October auction, do not pay extra for players whose main skill is two threes a game. Put that money into FG%, REB and BLK instead.

sections.heading: What the build gains and where it stops

paragraphs.text: Threes and FG% pull against each other. Giving up threes lets you chase FG% without that conflict. The limit is that in a big man build, only REB, BLK and FG% move together. Centers alone will not win you a week.

So the build needs guards and wings who also add steals and assists. Amen Thompson gives strong FG% on 13 shots a game plus rebounds, steals and blocks from a guard slot. Dyson Daniels is a steals specialist who also adds assists, rebounds and a good FG%. Ausar Thompson adds elite steals, solid blocks and rebounds. Late guards like Kevin Porter Jr. and Tre Jones add steals or assists without threes.

Spend your big money on the core. The notes put Amen Thompson at 35 to 38 USD, Jalen Duren at about 20 USD, and Ausar Thompson at 15 to 18 USD. They call Daniels a buy at anything under 20 USD. Duren gives elite FG% on volume and elite rebounds, and his FT% does little damage for a center. Do not chase him toward the higher site values.

In the middle rounds, add one or two centers who give FG%, REB and BLK. The fair ranges are about 8 to 12 USD for Jarrett Allen and Rudy Gobert, 10 to 14 USD for Ivica Zubac, 10 to 15 USD for Zach Edey and Cameron Boozer, about 6 USD for Zion Williamson, and 5 to 9 USD for Day'Ron Sharpe and Collin Murray-Boyles. Check playoff schedules too. Edey and Boozer have Memphis's 4-4-4 schedule. Gobert has a two-game week 20. Zubac plays 3-4-3 and Amen Thompson plays 3-3-4.

In the endgame, take cheap starting centers at 1 to 3 USD. Neemias Queta projects about 65% FG, 7.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks. Isaiah Hartenstein projects 61% FG and 9.7 rebounds. Jakob Poeltl, Yves Missi, Daniel Gafford, Isaiah Jackson, Moussa Diabaté, Nic Claxton and Paul Reed are all last-dollar options for FG% and blocks. Derik Queen is a 1 to 5 USD F/C flyer.

The sites disagree on whether some of these players are really non-shooters. Yahoo projects 1.3 threes a game for both Cameron Boozer and Yaxel Lendeborg, while ESPN projects 0.3. Yves Missi's FG% projection is 61.6% on Yahoo and 54.5% on ESPN. Treat these players as possible fits, not sure ones, and check their real numbers in the first weeks before you build around them.

Most bigs below the 144-player line are role or injury plays. Joan Beringer projects 12 points, 10 rebounds and 2.4 blocks if Gobert misses time. Robert Williams III is worth quick FAB if Clingan gets hurt or his minutes cap lifts. Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow matter when Embiid sits, and Marvin Bagley III matters when Jokic sits. Dereck Lively II is a FAB target if he wins the starting job after his return around Thanksgiving.

Plan for the playoffs too. Mark Williams could help a punt 3PM team in weeks 19 to 21 if he returns from his torn labrum in March, since Phoenix plays 4-4-4. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser has a 4-3-4 schedule and could return around Christmas. Hold him in an IL slot only for 1 USD.
